headline: Imaging Satellite Sent Into Orbit Exclusively To Track When My Neighbor Actually Water His Tulips
body:
The latest imaging satellite launched by the nation's space agency has officially reached its designated orbit, with mission control confirming that its primary objective is not climate monitoring or geological survey, but rather observing the backyard garden of a residence in suburban Bengaluru. The high-resolution sensor, capable of distinguishing individual petals from three hundred kilometers away, was activated this morning specifically to resolve a neighborhood dispute regarding the frequency of botanical care.

"We spent billions on the launch, the fuel, and the cryogenics just so we could finally settle whether the neighbor is actually watering his tulips on Tuesdays or just spraying the air to trick us," said the agency's lead payload engineer, who admitted the satellite's secondary function of mapping the entire Indian subcontinent was merely 'filler' to justify the flight time. The satellite is currently locked into a geostationary position that focuses solely on a 4-by-4-foot patch of soil, providing real-time data to a disgruntled local gardener.

Observers at the launch facility confirmed that the mission software has been modified to ignore all global data, with the main control screen currently displaying only a live feed of the aforementioned tulips. 'We tried to rotate the camera to see the Himalayas once,' one technician remarked, 'but the software threw a 'Priority Garden Priority' error code and immediately snapped back to the backyard. We’re just happy to provide scientific clarity to local lawn rivalries.'
caption: The sky is now occupied, and it is obsessed with your flower beds. Finally, technology serving the important issues. #ISRO #SpaceRace #GardenGoals (satire)

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 provides the most balanced satire, grounding the absurd technology of an imaging satellite in the mundane, relatable pettiness of a neighborhood gardening dispute. It avoids the repetitive 'I lost my keys' tropes found in the other candidates and maintains a consistent, deadpan voice throughout without over-explaining the joke.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses the premise of a neighbor's gardening habits for humorous exaggeration; no real-world private individuals are named, and the satire focuses on bureaucratic absurdity rather than targeting protected groups or individuals.
